title: Investigating key genes and molecular mechanisms of prostate cancer and coronary heart disease through transcriptomics and experimental validation.
authors: Wu, Ning; Gu, Hongchang; Qi, Zuo; Zhao, Zhiqiang; Cheng, Lijun; Wang, Yong; Liu, Zihao; Liu, Tong
one_liner_zh: 该研究通过转录组学和机器学习识别前列腺癌与冠心病共病关键基因，虽涉及TF关联和分子对接，但核心是疾病标志物筛选，非蛋白质-DNA互作机制建模，与本课题关联较弱。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Prostate cancer (PC), a common male urogenital malignancy, and coronary heart disease (CHD), a cardiovascular disease from coronary lesions causing myocardial ischemia, interact in comorbidity. This study integrated their transcriptome data to reveal comorbid mechanisms and develop cross-disease targets. METHODS: In this research, candidate genes were derived from differential analysis and intersection analysis. Subsequently, machine learning algorithms were integrated with receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve assessment and expression confirmation to identify key genes. Nomograms were further constructed, and analyses were carried out on the subcellular and chromosomal localization, enrichment pathways, molecular regulatory networks, and immune infiltration of these key genes. Potential drugs were predicted and molecular docking was performed. Ultimately, to confirm whether the expression patterns of key genes in clinical samples aligned with the bioinformatics analysis results, reverse transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR) was conducted. RESULTS: A total of 84 candidate genes were identified using bioinformatics approaches in this study. Through machine learning and validation with multiple datasets, ADD3 and ATP2B4 were identified as key genes, with good predictive performance. ADD3 is located on chromosome 10, and ATP2B4 is on chromosome 1. Both are distributed in the cell nucleus and are mainly enriched in ribosomes, ubiquitin-mediated protein degradation, and cancer-related pathways. ADD3 is associated with 21 micro RNAs (miRNAs) and 4 transcription factors (TFs), while ATP2B4 is associated with 11 miRNAs and 6 TFs. They are also involved in immune cell regulation. The study predicted 22 drugs, and molecular docking confirmed that they stably bound with potential drugs (e.g., DL-175) (docking score </=-5 kcal/moL). RT-qPCR results were consistent with bioinformatics analyses (P<0.05). CONCLUSIONS: This study determined the key genes related to PC and CHD, providing new bases and targets for diagnosis, treatment, and drug development.
abstract_zh: 背景：前列腺癌（PC）是一种常见的男性泌尿生殖系统恶性肿瘤，而冠心病（CHD）是由冠状动脉病变引起心肌缺血的心血管疾病，两者在共病中相互作用。本研究整合其转录组数据，以揭示共病机制并开发跨疾病靶点。方法：在本研究中，候选基因来源于差异分析和交集分析。随后，将机器学习算法与受试者工作特征（ROC）曲线评估及表达确认相结合，以识别关键基因。进一步构建了列线图，并对这些关键基因的亚细胞和染色体定位、富集通路、分子调控网络及免疫浸润进行了分析。预测了潜在药物并进行了分子对接。最终，为确认临床样本中关键基因的表达模式是否与生物信息学分析结果一致，进行了逆转录定量聚合酶链反应（RT-qPCR）。结果：本研究通过生物信息学方法共鉴定出84个候选基因。通过机器学习及多数据集验证，ADD3和ATP2B4被确定为关键基因，具有良好预测性能。ADD3位于10号染色体，ATP2B4位于1号染色体。两者均分布于细胞核中，主要富集于核糖体、泛素介导的蛋白质降解及癌症相关通路。ADD3与21个微小RNA（miRNAs）和4个转录因子（TFs）相关，而ATP2B4与11个miRNAs和6个TFs相关。它们还参与免疫细胞调控。研究预测了22种药物，分子对接确认它们与潜在药物（如DL-175）稳定结合（对接分数≤-5 kcal/mol）。RT-qPCR结果与生物信息学分析一致（P<0.05）。结论：本研究确定了与PC和CHD相关的关键基因，为诊断、治疗和药物开发提供了新依据和靶点。
